verdict.probe_answer: Both arms remove the per-param ordinal collision at the root by restoring a single ordered add_locals pass and attaching LocalFact afterward by def_byte. Both add an ambiguity-to-None regression. Arm A adds the ordinal regression in the existing name_resolution integration test path and resolves actual uses of a and b separately, so it is more likely to fail on the buggy code and to pin the intended resolver behavior. Arm B's ordinal test uses lookup_visible_binding at the same byte for both a and b; it still likely exposes the collision through the scope graph, but it is less direct and lives in the lower-level binding_lookup unit tests rather than the existing populate/resolve regression suite. Both fixes appear inert beyond the repair in the shown diff.
verdict.rationale: WRONG: no clear correctness defect in either implementation from the shown diff. Both implementation changes match the required single ordered binding pass: build a Vec of names from the collected facts, call add_locals once, then add per-binding facts keyed by def_byte. SMELL: neither diff shows verification of other add_locals call sites, but neither introduces broader changes and the task-provided diff only exposes bind_params. Arm A is materially better because its ordinal test asserts through single_file_resolve on separate source uses and Target::Local ordinals, matching the acceptance language more closely. Arm B is acceptable but its ordinal test is less targeted because it asks for both bindings at the same lookup byte and does not exercise the existing integration test helper.
